hints: For unequal class intervals, the height of each bar represents frequency density = frequency / class width.
Draw contiguous bars on the grid with boundaries at 0, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50 and label axes clearly with appropriate scales.
walkthrough:
Calculate the class width $w$ and frequency density $\text{fd} = \dfrac{f}{w}$ for each interval:
- $0 \le t < 5$: $w = 5, \; \text{fd} = \frac{23}{5} = 4.6$
- $5 \le t < 10$: $w = 5, \; \text{fd} = \frac{102}{5} = 20.4$
- $10 \le t < 20$: $w = 10, \; \text{fd} = \frac{135}{10} = 13.5$
- $20 \le t < 30$: $w = 10, \; \text{fd} = \frac{76}{10} = 7.6$
- $30 \le t < 50$: $w = 20, \; \text{fd} = \frac{24}{20} = 1.2$
Set up the horizontal axis for Time $t$ (minutes) from 0 to 50 and vertical axis for Frequency density from 0 to at least 21.
Draw rectangular bars across each interval matching the calculated frequency densities.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Recall the principle of a histogram.
In a histogram for grouped continuous data with unequal class widths, area is proportional to frequency:
$$\text{Frequency density} = \frac{\text{Frequency}}{\text{Class width}}$$

Step 2: Tabulate the class widths and frequency densities:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Time Interval } (t) & \text{Frequency } (f) & \text{Class Width } (w) & \text{Frequency Density } (\text{fd}) \\
\hline
[0, 5) & 23 & 5 & 23 / 5 = 4.6 \\
[5, 10) & 102 & 5 & 102 / 5 = 20.4 \\
[10, 20) & 135 & 10 & 135 / 10 = 13.5 \\
[20, 30) & 76 & 10 & 76 / 10 = 7.6 \\
[30, 50) & 24 & 20 & 24 / 20 = 1.2 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

Step 3: Plot on the grid.
- Label the vertical axis 'Frequency density' with a linear scale running from 0 to at least 21.
- Label the horizontal axis 'Time, $t$ (minutes)' with a linear scale from 0 to 50.
- Draw 5 contiguous bars spanning $[0,5]$ at height $4.6$, $[5,10]$ at height $20.4$, $[10,20]$ at height $13.5$, $[20,30]$ at height $7.6$, and $[30,50]$ at height $1.2$.

hints: Find the midpoint $t$ for each class interval: $2.5, 7.5, 15, 25, 40$.
Multiply each midpoint by its corresponding frequency and sum the products: $\sum f t$.
Divide by the total number of employees, $\sum f = 360$.
Evaluate $\dfrac{5707.5}{360}$ and give your answer to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Determine the midpoint of each class interval:
$$\text{Midpoints: } 2.5, \; 7.5, \; 15, \; 25, \; 40$$

Divide by the total frequency $\sum f = 360$ to estimate the mean:
$$\bar{t} = \frac{5707.5}{360} = 15.85416 \dots \approx 15.9\text{ minutes}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Find the midpoints of the intervals.
- $[0, 5)$: midpoint $t_1 = 2.5$
- $[5, 10)$: midpoint $t_2 = 7.5$
- $[10, 20)$: midpoint $t_3 = 15$
- $[20, 30)$: midpoint $t_4 = 25$
- $[30, 50)$: midpoint $t_5 = 40$

Step 3: Divide by total frequency $N = 360$:
$$\bar{t} = \frac{5707.5}{360} = \frac{11415}{720} = \frac{761}{48} = 15.85416 \dots$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $15.9$ minutes (or exact mixed fraction $15\frac{41}{48}$).
